text:
jessica (support): Hey team, customer AcmeCorp on Redwood Private is seeing intermittent API failures when going through their corporate proxy. They get CONNECT 200 then TLS handshake errors and 502/503 from our side. Need help triaging, they say it started after a proxy update last night.

alex (eng): Can you paste a minimal repro and the curl -v output? Also confirm whether they're using IP allowlist or egress allowlist for our endpoints.

jessica (support): Repro from customer (redacted):
```
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/ping
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/ping
*   Trying <proxy-ip>...
* Connected to corp-proxy.corp (proxy) port 3128 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.example.com:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com:443
> Proxy-Authorization: Basic <redacted>
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
< Proxy-Agent: SecuGate/3.2
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS alert, unknown CA (560):
* SSL: TLS: handshake failed
* Closing connection 0
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS alert, unknown CA (560):
* CONNECT failed: TLS handshake error
```
They see our SDK get 502/503 back after this.

sam (eng-networking): Looks like the proxy either doing TLS interception (unknown CA) or rewriting SNI/Host. Can you ask them to capture the proxy logs around the CONNECT? Specifically we need to see the raw CONNECT line and any subsequent bytes from the tunnel. Also ask them to run a client-side tcpdump to capture the TLS ClientHello so we can confirm SNI. Commands to ask them:
```
# reproduce with curl
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/ping 2>&1 | tee /tmp/curl.log
# capture traffic to proxy
sudo tcpdump -i any host corp-proxy.corp and port 3128 -w /tmp/proxy.pcap
# or capture client hello bytes
sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/clienthello.pcap 'tcp and (port 443)'
```

maria (eng-sre): Two common failure modes: (A) transparent proxy / SSL inspection replacing certs (customer must install corp CA) which often yields "unknown CA" or handshake failures; (B) proxy rewrites SNI or the CONNECT target header, causing our server to receive mismatched SNI => server selects a different cert or closes. We should ask AcmeCorp to check SecuGate's SSL-bump config: is it set to 'bump' for all TLS vs 'splice/pass-through' for CONNECT to our domains?

eng-oncall: Temporary mitigation: if they can add an egress rule to bypass the proxy for api.redwood.example.com (or add an explicit passthrough for port 443) that will confirm if proxy is root cause. If bypassing fixes it, provider needs to change proxy policy rather than us.

acme-netops: From our side: we captured the proxy session. After CONNECT we see the proxy returns 200 then it injects an extra header and then forwards a ClientHello where the SNI is set to "proxy.corp" (not api.redwood.example.com). Hex snippet (trimmed):
```
0000  43 4f 4e 4e 45 43 54 20 61 70 69 2e 72 65 64 77 6f 6f 64 2e 65 78 61 6d 70 6c 65 2e 63 6f 6d 3a 34 34 33 20 48 54 54 50 2f 31 2e 31 0d 0a
...
000d  16 03 01 02 00 01 00 01 fc 03 03 5b 90 ... // TLS ClientHello
000f  ... 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 0b 00 13 70 72 6f 78 79 2e 63 6f 72 70
```
So the ClientHello being seen by our edge has SNI = "proxy.corp". We did a quick test bypassing the proxy and TLS handshake succeeds.

alex (eng): That nails it — the proxy is rewriting SNI or performing active TLS interception and not preserving target SNI. When the SNI is wrong the server picks a mismatched cert or closes the handshake which manifests as TLS/503 downstream.

eng-security: If they have an inspection appliance that re-terminates TLS, they must either: 1) install the corp CA in their clients so the re-signed certs are trusted; OR 2) configure the proxy to allow passthrough for api.redwood.example.com (no MITM). For privacy/compliance use-cases we also offer a Private deployment with egress options that avoid customer-wide MITM.

maria (eng-sre): Action items for AcmeCorp:
- Provide proxy logs for the CONNECT session (timestamp 2026-03-16 03:12:xx)
- Provide the tcpdump/pcap capturing the ClientHello to confirm SNI (pcap sanitized ok)
- Temporarily bypass proxy for our host to confirm baseline (they already said bypass fixes it)
- If they need inspection, configure their proxy to preserve SNI and not rewrite Host in CONNECT tunnels (or add an allowlist)

support-bot: KB: https://redwood.internal.kb/proxy-troubleshooting "HTTP CONNECT + TLS interception" (internal) :eyes:

jessica (support): I'll ask AcmeCorp for the pcaps and proxy config screenshots. They said they pushed a SecuGate update last night that enabled "SNI rewrite" by default.

acme-netops: Confirmed: SecuGate was set to rewrite SNI to internal proxy hostname for inspection. We switched it off for a test and everything passed. We'll roll a config change to whitelist redwood domains.

sam (eng-networking): Great — once they whitelist/passthrough for our domain, ask them to verify with curl again and send us the curl log. Also if they prefer, we can provide a static IP allowlist for their Dedicated/Private endpoint to make allowlisting simpler.

jessica (support): Customer happy to change config. Marking this as resolved for now, will update if they see regressions. :thumbsup:

alex (eng): Nice win. Add a short note to the KB about "SecuGate SNI rewrite causing CONNECT handshake failures" with the tcpdump excerpt.

eng-oncall: Closing loop: recommend adding monitoring alert for increased TLS handshake failures from a single customer IP range so we can detect proxy-related regressions earlier. :mag_right:

eng-security: Also flag for sales/solutions: when onboarding Private deployments, document proxy SSL inspection gotchas and recommended config snippets for common appliances (SecuGate, BlueProxy, CorpMITM).

jessica (support): Closing thread — will reopen if AcmeCorp reports more issues.
